['Helička was not proud, not proud, yet she came to our feast, came: Heličko! Heličko! Smooth your golden cheek, hop on your bare little foot, choose a bridesmaid from the circle, from the rose a blossom, from the rose a blossom, the one that would suit you best. Now the circle will remain standing, Helička will take one bridesmaid from it and dance three times with her in the circle, during which the other bridesmaids, standing, sing as follows: Over mountains, over valleys, over waters, over forests, hey little ball, you golden quince! Let go of that bridesmaid, stay in the circle. Then Helička leads the bridesmaid back to her previous place in the circle, stands again in the middle, and the bridesmaids, beginning to turn around her again, sing as at the beginning: Helička was not proud, etc. Now Helička takes the second girl in the circle to dance, and then the third, and so on one after another, until she has replaced them all, which ends the game. In practice, the children deviate from this order of the game by having Helička, after dancing with a bridesmaid, leave her in her place in the circle and herself, becoming a bridesmaid, turn with the others around the new Helička; in this way, everyone takes turns. However, this is against the rule of the song itself, which explicitly commands Helička to let go of the bridesmaid and remain in the circle herself.', '1. Yesterday the sun was shining for me, today it no longer shines for me, I loved a girl, she was like a flower. God, she was a girl, she had blue eyes, I used to take her for a walk in the green grove.  
2. We walked around the little grove three times, I did not complain, my darling cried, I howled. Don’t cry, my darling, the cloth means nothing to you, tomorrow they will take me to Brno, I will already be drafted.  
3. When we arrived in Brno, there were soldiers there, they had green insignia, they were hunters. One of them told me to join them too, I was a little drunk, I did it.  
4. When I woke up in the morning, I already regretted it, my darling cried, it was all in vain. Don’t cry, my darling, the cloth means nothing to you, and I have to be a soldier, the end of love.  
5. When we said goodbye under the green oak, we always told each other that we would not be each other’s anymore. I have to go far away, across the wide sea, and I will no longer see your blue eyes.', '1. One day during the war, a little soldier stood guard, not far away in a green grove a nightingale sang a song.  
2. Be silent, nightingale, and do not sing, you awaken sorrow in my heart, you remind me of those happy moments when I used to walk with Milka.  
3. When I used to walk with my Milka, the moon shone on us, that nightingale in the green grove sang a beautiful song.  
4. There we sat together on the green grass, I picked flowers for her, and she wove a wreath of tender flowers for me.  
5. When she had woven the wreath, entwined with rosemary, she gave me her right hand, saying farewell, goodbye.  
6. And when we parted, I took to the path, my heart still aches with sorrow when I remember everything.  
7. On the first day, early in the morning, a dispatch came for me that I must go to the regiment and leave everything behind.  
8. On the second day, early in the morning, I hear drummers beating, the general on his black horse began to command.  
9. On the third day, early in the morning, I hear buglers sounding, the general on his black horse begins to lead the war.  
10. Rise, brothers with rifles, a cloud covers the sky, then a burning bullet flies, piercing my chest.  
11. Blood runs in streams from the wound; I stopped it with my finger, once more shouted for the last time: Farewell, Milka! And died.']

Representative_Docs: ['II. When girls play the Water Sprite, who of course is also a girl, their game differs from the previous boys\' game only in their different activities in the water and different verses. The girls, upon coming to the shore, ask the Water Sprite: Water Sprite, Tatrmánek! reveal yourself: can we wash diapers in this pond? The Water Sprite replies the first and second time, "I do not allow it!" and only when asked for the third time does he answer in a hoarse voice: You may, wash and rinse; just leave my little fish to me.', 'For the goslings. The same game as the boys’: “At the Golden Gate.” Two girls imitate a gate, standing opposite each other and holding hands raised so that there is a passage underneath. One of them calls herself the Sun, the other the Moon. From afar comes a line of girls, the “goslings,” one after another, holding each other by the hips over their skirts; the first called the “gosling boy.” Gate: Goslings, goslings, fly! Goslings: We must not. Gate: For whom? Goslings: For the lord. Gate: The lord is not home, he went to Beroun, for a white ram with golden horns. The goslings fly toward the gate, shouting: “Honk! honk! honk!” And when the last in line tries to fly through, the gate closes, and the gosling gets caught between the Sun and the Moon. Gate: Gosling, where have you been? Gosling: In the forest. Gate: What were you doing there? Gosling: Cutting wood. Gate: What for the wood? Gosling: For the garden. Gate: What for the garden? Gosling: To plant lettuce. Gate: What for the lettuce? Gosling: To have food. Gate: For that you must, gosling, be ours. Whom will you choose: the Sun or the Moon? The gosling answers and stands behind the one she chooses. Then the gate calls again: Goslings, goslings, fly! Goslings: “We must not,” and so on, as at first. When all the goslings, including the gosling boy, have joined either the Sun or the Moon, the “Suns” and “Moons” begin to fight, each side straining to pull the other over the line, in every way, just like in the boys’ game: “At the Golden Gate.” See also Krol. I, 295. – Suš. 729. – 1) Also: for precious roots, for heart aches.', 'II. Two boys first secretly agree between themselves who will be the Angel and who will be the Devil, and with a half-step they make a gate, but each only with one hand. The other boys, holding hands, form a circle in the gate, so that one pillar of the gate is inside the circle and the other pillar is outside the circle. The circle begins to turn, and the Devil and the Angel sing as follows: Under the pit, a mouse, under the pit: come, you tomcat, come with us! The keys ring, the violet scents. The gate is open, supported by a sword: whoever touches the gate shall be beheaded. Slash! Slash! Slash! At the word “slash!” the arch is lowered for the first and second time always between two boys in the circle, and immediately lifted again; but at the third time the circle stops, and the gate asks the one in front of whom the arch was lowered: “Whom do you join?” He then answers: “You,” pointing to one or the other, not knowing whether he joined the Angel or the Devil, and stands behind him. Then the circle closes again, starts to turn, and the gate sings as in the beginning: Under the pit, a mouse, etc. This goes on until even the last one in the circle has joined either one or the other side of the gate.
